result.title: CoRD: Coupled Rollouts Fill the Blind Spot of On-Policy Distillation
result.summary: On-policy distillation trains a student on its own rollouts, so states the teacher would reach but the student does not are seldom supervised. We introduce CoRD (coupled-rollout distillation), which keeps the on-policy loss and moves only the distribution of training states toward the teacher, drawing rollouts from a geometric interpolation of student and teacher through the maximal coupling of speculative decoding. The coupling keeps the student's token wherever the two distributions agree and otherwise substitutes a token from the part of the target the student underweights, so interventions are as rare as any exact sampler allows and recede as the student learns. Across six base students from two model families (Qwen3 and Qwen3.5, 0.6B to 4B), CoRD raises average pass@1 over on-policy distillation by 0.9 to 2.0 points and pass@8 by 1.2 to 3.4 points on five public math benchmarks at equal steps and data. On frozen teacher-reached states, a 4B student trained with CoRD reaches in 16 steps a gap closure that on-policy distillation does not reach in 80, and substitution rules intervening at least as often in other directions fall short of CoRD.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CoRD：保留 on-policy 蒸馏损失，仅将训练状态的分布通过 student 与 teacher 的几何插值及 speculative decoding 的极大耦合推向教师，使干预尽量稀疏并随学生变好而减少，在五个数学基准上提升 pass@1 与 pass@8。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「学生自采样状态覆盖不到教师可达状态」的诊断与按需替换 token 的轨迹构造，或可供核查 LVR 中 latent 轨迹训练的状态分布覆盖与监督分配问题；但该工作为纯文本蒸馏，与视觉证据或 latent 推理状态无直接联系，迁移性需进一步判断。
